question: Which of the following is the major river that flows across the western part of Rajasthan?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Luni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Luni River:

 
 
• The Luni River is an important river in Rajasthan, India. It originates in the Aravalli Range near Ajmer and flows southwestwards through the Thar Desert.
 
• Unlike many rivers, the Luni River does not flow into a sea or ocean. Instead, it ends in the marshy lands of the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat, making it an inland draining river.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Ghaggar**

 
 
• The Ghaggar River rises in Shivalik hills in the Solan district of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• It enters Haryana from the Panchkula district.
 
• Then after the river flows making the border between Punjab and Haryana for more than 100 Km.
 
• And at the end, the river leaves Sirsa District of Haryana State and reaches Sri Ganga Nagar district, Rajasthan.
 
 
 
• **​Chambal**
 
 
• The Chambal river originates in Manpura near Indore in Madhya Pradesh.__
 
• The length of the river is 900 km and it is a tributary of Yamuna river.
 
• The Chambal River remains one of North India’s unpolluted rivers, home to a rich diversity of flora and fauna.
 
• The National Chambal Gharial Wildlife Sanctuary is famous for the rare Ganges river dolphin.
 
• Apart from the Ganges river dolphin, the other inhabitants of the sanctuary include magar (crocodile) and gharial (alligator). Migratory birds from Siberia form part of its rich avian fauna.
 
 
 
• **Banas**
 
 
• Banas river originates from Khamnor Hills of Aravalli Range, near Kumbhalgarh in Rajsamand, Rajasthan. '
 
• Banas river is a tributary of the Chambal River and ii is approximately 512 kilometers in length.
 
• This river is also called ‘Van Ki Asha‘.
 
• There is another river in Rajasthan with the name of Banas.
 
• The Banas river entirely flows within the Rajasthan in:-
 
 
• Ajmer, Bhilwara, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Dausa, Jaipur, Pali, Rajsamand, Sawai Madhopur, Sirohi, Tonk, and Udaipur districts of Rajasthan. 
 
 
 
• It flows northeast through the Mewar region of Rajasthan and meets the Chambal near the village of Rameshwar in Sawai Madhopur district.
